elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 15.9 selects the internal laws of the State of Delaware, not New York.

elements.element: The state courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 15.10.1 instead designates state courts located in the State of Delaware.

elements.element: The federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 15.10.1 instead designates federal courts located in the State of Delaware.

elements.element: The selected governing law is Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, an expressly permitted fallback.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, Delaware courts are designated as the judicial forum.
elements.evidence: Section 15.10.1 requires unresolved Disputes, including intellectual-property disputes, to be brought exclusively in Delaware state and federal courts, subject to the stated special-dispute, preliminary-relief, and mutually agreed arbitration provisions.

elements.element: If California law is selected, California courts are designated as the judicial forum.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects Delaware rather than California law.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, the courts of London are designated as the judicial forum.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects Delaware rather than the laws of England and Wales.

result.reason: The redline does not satisfy the New York preferred position, but it implements the Delaware fallback by retaining Delaware governing law and designating Delaware state and federal courts as the exclusive general judicial forum. Conditioning ICDR arbitration on later mutual written agreement is directly related and appropriately conforms the arbitration provisions. The existing special-dispute and preliminary-injunction carveouts are preserved. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 15.10.2.2 ends with an incomplete sentence.
